name: Digital Protocols and AI Protocol Design
blurb: Moving protocols from documents to structured data.
title: Digital Protocols and AI Protocol Design
answer: Document based protocols are slow to write and a leading cause of amendments. The industry is moving to structured, digital protocols that AI can check for feasibility and that flow directly into trial systems, which also makes AI drafting and review more reliable.

reading.body:
Document based clinical protocols are slow to write and a leading cause of amendments, and the fix is structured digital protocols that AI can check and that flow directly into trial systems.

The pattern is a change of format, not a change of method. A protocol written as a document is readable by people and awkward for software. A protocol written as structured data can be tested for feasibility before it is fixed, and can move into trial systems without being retyped. IQVIA described this shift in April 2026 as building AI ready trials through digital protocols that replace document centric designs.

The payoff is stated twice over: fewer amendments, and AI tools that can actually read the design. That second point is the one that matters for AI specifically. Drafting and review tools are only as reliable as the material they operate on, and a structured protocol gives them fields and constraints rather than prose to interpret. The same structure that makes a design machine checkable makes machine drafting and review more dependable.

What the data does not cover is scale. It gives one vendor's account and no counts of amendments avoided, no time saved, no measure of how far the industry has actually moved. It also says nothing about compute, buildings, or power, and nothing here should be read as a claim about them. The argument is about data format inside life sciences, and it stands or falls there.

sections.body: Structured protocol data pays off twice: fewer amendments and AI tools that can actually read the design.
